blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — bevacizumab perioperative wound-healing precaution
stem: A client receiving bevacizumab (AVASTIN) is scheduled for elective major surgery. Which preoperative medication plan is consistent with the current prescribing information?

options.A: Withhold bevacizumab for at least 28 days before the elective surgery because the medication is associated with surgery and wound-healing complications.
options.B: Continue bevacizumab through the day of surgery because perioperative exposure does not increase wound-healing complications and no preoperative interval is needed.
options.C: Hold bevacizumab on the morning of surgery and resume it the next day if vital signs are stable, because a one-day interruption is the labeled precaution.
options.D: Increase bevacizumab before surgery to reduce postoperative bleeding and improve wound healing, then continue the usual dosing schedule after the procedure.

rationale: Current AVASTIN labeling identifies surgery and wound-healing complications as a serious risk and directs clinicians to withhold AVASTIN for at least 28 days before elective surgery. It also states not to administer AVASTIN for at least 28 days after major surgery and until adequate wound healing. Therefore A is correct. B ignores the labeled perioperative risk, C uses an insufficient interruption and premature restart, and D proposes an unsupported dose increase that conflicts with the wound-healing precaution.
educational_objective: Apply the labeled bevacizumab perioperative safety rule: withhold AVASTIN for at least 28 days before elective surgery and recognize that post-major-surgery dosing is also delayed for at least 28 days and until adequate wound healing.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_version_date: Current DailyMed version 39 verified and accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Dosage and Administration §2.1/§2.9 and Warnings and Precautions §5.2 Surgery and Wound Healing Complications: withhold for at least 28 days prior to elective surgery; do not administer for at least 28 days following major surgery and until adequate wound healing.
source_claim_supported: Bevacizumab should be withheld for at least 28 days before elective surgery because of wound-healing complications; after major surgery, administration is delayed at least 28 days and until adequate wound healing.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: identify medication precautions and adverse effects; administer medications safely; monitor client response.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as plausible perioperative medication plans without the original absolute-word cue.
Preserved the exact source-supported 28-day preoperative interval and balanced option length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current AVASTIN perioperative labeling. B, C, and D conflict with the wound-healing precaution; the 28-day interval is directly supported rather than inferred.
